title.narrative: COVID-19: Health System Enhancement to Address and Limit COVID-19

description.narrative: As part of the comprehensive support of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for the Government of the Philippines in responding to the coronavirus disease (COVID-19), HEAL will assist the Department of Health (DOH) in scaling up public health capacity to manage the pandemic.

description.narrative: Capacity of DOH to detect, contain, and treat COVID-19 cases strengthened

Mortality rate from COVID-19 Progress/Status: The mortality rate for 2020-2024 is less than 1%.
The cumulative COVID-19 case fatality rate from January 2020 to 31 December 2024, is 1.61% (male: 1.84% and female: 1.40%), or 67,192 (male: 37,082 and female: 30,110) reported deaths out of the 4,164,645 cases (male: 2,017,074 and female: 2,147,570). Data Source: DOH records Actual value:

The overall test positivity rate of COVID-19 confirmed cases Progress/Status: As discussed during the MTR, the policy for conducting PCR tests was revised in early 2022. It is no longer accurate to use COVID-19 positive rates to measure the country's COVID-19 situation. During the MTR, it was agreed that this outcome indicator needs to be revised. ADB and DOH will continue to discuss this matter.
As of 31 December 2024, the utilization rate for the total number of ICU beds for COVID-19 is 10.63%. For non-ICU beds, the total hospital bed utilization ranged is 13.17%. Data Source: DOH records Actual value:

Average turnaround time from sample collection to test results Progress/Status: DOH reported an average turnaround time from 30.43 hours in January 2021 to 20.71 hours in December 2024. Data Source: Laboratory records Baseline value: 48-72 hours
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Treatment capacity for COVID-19 scaled up Indicator: At least 75% of emergency, admission, and ICU health care workers have increased capacity to deliver psycho-social support to patients and their families during public health outbreaks, including pregnant women and disadvantaged people Progress/Status: Pilot training of psycho-social support to patients and their families were conducted in 14-17 December 2021.Training was rolled out in Subic (May 2022) and Cebu (June 2022). A total of 115 participants from hospitals and facilities supported by the project took part of the training program. Data Source: Hospital records and project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Treatment capacity for COVID-19 scaled up Indicator: Total number of fully functional ventilators nationwid Progress/Status: As of 31 December 2024, the average number of available mechanical ventilators nationwide is now at 6,248. HEAL procured 90 mechanical ventilators installed in 55 recipient hospitals. Data Source: Hospital records of ventilator use Actual value:

Output: Disease surveillance and diagnostic capacity upgraded Indicator: Number of government molecular laboratories conducting COVID-19 PCR testing Progress/Status: The project increased its support to public health laboratories across the country by providing 51 units of RT-PCR machines (100% delivered). Additionally, 45 CT Scans, 85 portable x-rays, and 85 patient transfer vehicles were delivered. 3,465 units of 4,091 (85%) have been delivered and installed at the recipient facilities Data Source: DOH and hospital records Actual value:

Output: Infection prevention and control measures expanded Indicator: The percentage of health workers infected with COVID-19 Progress/Status: As of 30 December 2024, the total number of COVID-19 positive cases among health workers is 29,964. There is a downward trend of COVID-19 cases among HCW from the baseline to present. The rate of positive cases among health workers was 0.64% as of 31 December 2023. Data Source: Hospital records Actual value:

Output: Disease surveillance and diagnostic capacity upgraded Indicator: At least 75% of staff (50% or more female) in each project-supported laboratory meet the National Laboratory Biosafety Competency Requirements Progress/Status: Of the 120 target participants, a total of 237(197%) laboratory staff from the target facilities completed the National Laboratory Biosafety Competency Requirements with 174 (73.4%) female and 63 (26.6%) male participants. More than 75% of the staff of project-supported facilities are competent on National Laboratory Competency where 50% (of 75%) are female by 2022. The target of this indicator was achieved. Data Source: Laboratory biosafety training and assessment reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Target year: 2022 Target value: =<75%

Output: Disease surveillance and diagnostic capacity upgraded Indicator: More than 50,000 COVID-19 tests conducted per day Progress/Status: As of 31 December 2024, the number of provinces with at least 1 functional PCR laboratory has been increased to 57 compared to baseline data of “0” as of 20 July 2020 (total of 215 licensed and operational PCR laboratories in the country). Data Source: Laboratory records and results Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: 22,500 Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: 22,500 Target year: 2020 Target value: <50,000

Output: Infection prevention and control measures expanded Indicator: Capacity of isolation wards Progress/Status: As of 30 September 2025, out of 13 facilities, five sites (San Lazaro Hospital, Lung Center of the Philippines, Jose B. Lingad Regional Memorial Hospital, Western Visayas Medical Center, and Davao Regional Medical Center) have progressed from 75% and above. Four sites (Ilocos Training and Regional Medical Center, Luis Hora memorial Medical Center, Bataan General Hospital and Medical Center, and Batangas Medical Center) have progressed to 51% to 74%. Two sites (Northern Mindanao Medical Center and Mariveles Mental Wellness and General Hospital have progressed to 26% to 50%, while 2 sites (Dr Paulino J. Garcia Memorial Research and Medical Center, and Southern Philippines Medical Center) remain below 25%. Data Source: Hospital records of bed use (regular wards and ICUs), community records Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Target year: 2022 Target value: 100

Output: Infection prevention and control measures expanded Indicator: Health care workers in obstetrics, pediatrics, and emergency departments of supported hospitals have increased awareness and knowledge on maternal and child health guidelines during public health outbreaks Progress/Status: A total of 113 health care workers with 76.99% of females trained on maternal and child health guidelines. This was beyond the target of 108 workers. A total of 47 (female 36; male 11) health care workers from the project facilities participated in the batch 1 training on “infection Prevention and Control for Covid-19 for health care workers delivering maternal and child health services” which was held on 12 to 16 October 2022. In addition, a total of 66 health care workers with 51 females participated in the second batch of the training on 20-24 October 2022. Data Source: Project training records, production, and distribution of communication leaflets Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Target year: 2023 Target value: 75%

Output: Infection prevention and control measures expanded Indicator: Supply of at least 3 million doses of safe and effective COVID-19 vaccines assured by the end of March 2021 (December 2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: HEAL funded a portion of the advance payment for the procurement of 40M doses of COVID-19 vaccines. HEAL also funded the procurement of ancillaries (diluents, mixing syringes, and microsyringes) for the 40M doses of COVID-19 vaccines. In 2024, the reconciliation of the inventory was completed and there are no unaccounted distributions. Data Source: DOF and DOH records, project progress reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2021 Target value: 3 million

Output: Treatment capacity for COVID-19 scaled up Indicator: At least 75% of health care workers in the emergency departments of project hospitals report increased knowledge and awareness of how to detect and support victims of gender-based violence Progress/Status: A total of 112 healthcare workers from project-supported facilities participated in the training program for Detection and Assistance to Victims-Survivors of Gender-Based Violence during COVID-19 Pandemic and Future Public Health Outbreak Data Source: Hospital records and project progress reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: TBD Target year: 2023 Target value: 75%
